data.title: Phillips 66 shares uptick after eight-session losing streak
data.description:
Phillips 66 (PSX) shares snapped eight straight sessions of losses, as the stock was up 1.78% at $240.29 on Friday.

The integrated downstream energy company fell about 9.4% in the preceding six sessions. PSX is down 11% over the past one month, while the stock has risen over 88% so far this year, compared to a 5% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index (SP500).

"PSX's stock appears optically cheap on trailing multiples, but the current price ($260) already embeds optimistic assumptions about sustainable refining margins and Midstream growth. The upside depends on PSX sustaining higher normalized refining margins or Midstream outperformance; downside risk emerges if margins revert or infrastructure returns disappoint," pointed out a recent Seeking Alpha analysis.

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, PSX has a Strong Buy rating with a score of 4.97 out of 5. The company received an A in the prospect of profitability, while it got an A+ in the growth factor.

Turning to the Wall Street community, eleven analysts gave PSX a Buy and above rating. Eight analysts have given the stock a Hold recommendation, while one recommended Sell.

Seeking Alpha analysts are cautious and see the stock as a Hold.

data.title: XPENG launches five new vehicle models, megawatt charging infrastructure
data.description:
At the Guangzhou Auto Show on Friday, XPENG (XPEV) unveiled its plans for production of a humanoid robot XPENG IRON as a customer-facing store assistant at its XPENG showrooms, as well as the establishment of a Hong Kong research and development facility to expand its X-Energy megawatt charging infrastructure.

The Chinese automaker is also expanding its vehicle lineup with five new models for 2027.

Beginning in December 2026, XPENG (XPEV) will launch the XPENG L05, a five-seat, intelligent SUV in Thailand, with a European launch planned at the Brussels Motor Show in January 2027.

In 2027, the company will then introduce five new models, including the P7 in Europe, planned for the second quarter of the year.

“We aim to more than double our overseas vehicle sales in 2027,” said Alex Tang, XPENG’s vice president of international business.

To facilitate its vehicle expansion, the company is accelerating the deployment of its X-Energy megawatt charging infrastructure. X-Energy can deliver up to 1K kW of peak power with a grid connection of no more than 240 kW, reducing the pressure on local power grids and helping increase energy capabilities in densely populated urban areas with limited space for power grids.

Finally, XPENG (XPEV) is accelerating the development of its advanced driver-assistance technology and purpose-built robotaxi. 

“As XPENG enters its next phase of global growth, its international strategy is evolving beyond intelligent vehicles to encompass a broader ecosystem of physical AI technologies. Through AI vehicles, humanoid robots, and Robotaxis, XPENG aims to bring the benefits of AI into everyday life for people around the world,” the company said in a press release.

Shares closed nearly 4% higher on Friday.

data.title: Baron Financials ETF adds Dave, JPMorgan, and AerCap; exits Baldwin Insurance and Fair Isaac

data.title: M&A lift: Home Depot and Lowe's are hammering out post-deal synergies
data.description:
Home improvement giants Home Depot (HD) and Lowe's (LOW) updated investors and analysts during their recent earnings conference calls on how their biggest acquisitions are helping them win more business from professional contractors.

Home Depot (HD) bought SRS Distribution, which serves roofers, landscapers, and pool contractors, for $18.3B in 2024. SRS has since added GMS and the HVAC distributor Mingledorff's. It now runs five business lines from more than 1.3K locations. SRS's third-quarter sales rose 25.1% to $4.87 billion, helped by those acquisitions. Its mix is also more balanced. Roofing fell to about 38% of SRS sales from 50% a year earlier, so the business depends less on storm-driven demand, which may appeal to investors.

Looking ahead, Home Depot's (HD) biggest opportunity may be selling more of its products to SRS customers. "We're on track to meet the $400 million goal that we laid out for 2026, and we look to double that in 2027," highlighted Mike Rowe, Home Depot's (HD) executive vice president of Pro. Customers that used to buy in one category are now buying across several. Home Depot (HD) plans to open 40 to 50 new SRS branches this year.

Meanwhile, Lowe's (LOW) responded to Home Depot's (HD) aggressive M&A moves with an agreement to buy Foundation Building Materials, a distributor of interior building products, for approximately $8.8B. That deal is already producing savings, according to CFO Brandon Sink, who noted the purchasing benefits in drywall, steel, and insulation were largely realized in 2026 and will carry into 2027. Plans to increase sales are still being tested, which leaves room for more gains. They include selling Lowe's products to FBM customers and letting those customers use their FBM credit in Lowe's stores. Sink noted excess cash can pay for most of FBM's 15 planned new branches and small acquisitions, while paying down debt stays a priority for the company.  Lowe's (LOW) will give more detail on FBM at an investor conference on December 9.

data.title: Nasdaq rises 7% on Thanksgiving week, bolstered by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) saw a volatile run in the holiday-shortened week, with the index closing 2.31% higher on Friday.

On Monday, the tech-heavy index shot up over 6% following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO. However, Nasdaq faced renewed selling pressure in the following session, reversing its previous gains.

With markets shut on Thursday on account of Thanksgiving Day, the index rose 6.68% for the week.

Semiconductor stocks made up for the majority of the decliners this week, with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) leading the list. Meanwhile, Axon Enterprise (AXON) and Moderna (MRNA) were among the top gainers.

data.title: S&P 500 posts weekly gains as Wall Street rebounds from steep losses
data.description:
Wall Street finished on top on Black Friday as the major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week.

The blue-chip Dow closed up 1.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) advanced 1.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite rose 2.3%.

The S&P 500 gained 5.6% for the week following a decline of 8.61% the previous week.

Seeking Alpha analyst Agar Capital noted that it was the shortest week of the year but also the longest psychologically. Everything happened in just a few sessions, with low volumes and incredibly violent index movements.

The analyst highlighted that it all started with Jensen Huang's return on Monday, followed by the selloff and then the final recovery.

On the macroeconomic front, the economy still appears strong, while the analyst said that, regarding the new tariff threats, they appeared to be more of a blank bullet, at least for now.

“Personally, at these price levels, I have regained confidence. The risk-reward ratio has widened in favor of the investor, and I must admit that I am especially encouraged by the fact that the recovery has affected all eleven sectors of the S&P 500. Certainly, the covering of bearish positions and low liquidity have amplified the movement. But after weeks in which it seemed that not even good news could support the markets, something seems to be changing. Earnings and earnings expectations remain strong, so I believe there are reasons to approach the coming weeks with greater optimism,” Agar Capital concluded.

From a sector-level perspective, all 11 S&P 500 sectors ended the week in positive territory after last week's steep losses.

Materials (XLB) and Communication Services (XLC) were the biggest gainers, rising 7.92% and 7.48%, respectively.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman was not surprised to see the rebound this week following last week's selloff.

He added that there's only so much selling that can be done. However, he said it was interesting to see where the rebound took place.

“We saw aggressive sectors run much higher than defensive sectors. Big tech, spread across communications, consumer discretionary, and technology, all gained more than defensive sectors like staples and utilities. This is a good thing for the bulls because it is a risk-on signal, especially with a cyclical sector like materials at the helm. But investors should stay cautious; one week does not mark a new regime. This bounce was catalyzed by the oversold conditions from the week prior. We have yet to see if this bull still has its legs,” Bowman concluded.

On the other hand, Utilities (XLU) and Energy (XLE) posted the smallest weekly gains, advancing 2.34% and 2.06%, respectively.
